goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — update` looks up the host by id without a nil check before calling `save_host`, which immediately calls `.host=` and raises NoMethodError for a bad/stale id instead of returning 404.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If the id is stale/invalid, `host` will be nil. `save_host` immediately dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), which will raise a NoMethodError instead of returning a 404/not_found response. This is a concrete correctness bug present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:60 — The `delete` action's `destroyRecord()` call has no `.catch`, so a failed delete is silently swallowed with no user feedback, unlike `save` which handles errors.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` but does not attach a `.catch(...)`. If the DELETE request fails (network/server error), the promise rejection is not handled here and no `popupAjaxError` (or any feedback) is shown, unlike the `save()` action which explicitly does `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. This is directly verifiable in the diff and constitutes a real error-handling/UX defect.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the only admin model types involved are 'site_customization' (one underscore) and 'embeddable_host' (one underscore), which become 'site-customization' and 'embeddable-host' with a single replace and will correctly match entries in ADMIN_MODELS. The proposed issue only manifests for types containing multiple underscores, but no such types are added or referenced in this change, so there is no verifiable defect introduced by the diff.
